methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective survivorship cohort study with longitudinal follow-up. Sample size and power calculation not apparent from excerpt. Outcome assessment methods (patient-reported, clinical) documented but reliability/validity not specified. Confounding variables identified but adjustment methodology not fully detailed. Attrition/loss-to-follow-up rates not characterized.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Prospective cohort study (LoE: 2b) investigating cancer survivor health outcomes (physical, psychosocial, functional). Clinically relevant: identifies burden of long-term treatment effects and supports survivorship care planning. However, observational design limits causal inferences regarding interventions.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE prospective cohort reporting: baseline characteristics, outcome definitions, follow-up procedures described. Gaps: detailed methods regarding patient-reported outcome instrument validation/administration, missing data handling, complete follow-up rates not specified, data sharing statement absent.

novelty_literature.justification: Describes cancer survivor health outcomes; addresses important clinical question but findings largely confirmatory of known survivorship challenges (fatigue, psychosocial burden). Incremental contribution without novel intervention or mechanistic insight.

writing_presentation.justification: Prospective cohort report with standard organization. Results systematically presented but methodological clarity could be improved.

key_strengths: Prospective design: longitudinal follow-up minimizes recall bias compared to cross-sectional designs
Addresses clinical need: cancer survivor health outcomes inform supportive care strategies
key_concerns: Methodological gaps: power calculation, confounding adjustment methods, attrition rates not transparent
Limited novelty: findings mostly confirmatory of known survivorship challenges
Causality unclear: observational design cannot attribute outcomes to specific treatments or factors without intervention trials
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 paper: prospective survivorship cohort study requiring major revisions addressing methodological transparency and clinical intervention implications.
